WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords", and had the gold and silver vessels from the temple at Jerusalem brought in to drink from. Daniel 5:1–3
Daniel to the king: "thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this". Daniel 5:22
"TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting." Daniel 5:27
"In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain." Daniel 5:30
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
The vessels of the house of God were used at his feast while the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood and stone were praised. Daniel 5:3–4 Daniel 5:23
Daniel: "Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians." Daniel 5:28
He made Daniel, "of the children of the captivity of Judah", the third ruler in the kingdom. Daniel 5:13 Daniel 5:29

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
DOUGHERTY (1929): KINGSHIP ENTRUSTED TO HIM
Entrusted with the kingship in Nabonidus's third year (553 BC) and acting as co-regent, on Dougherty's view, until Babylon fell in 539.
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Daniel 7:1 is dated "in the first year of Belshazzar" and Daniel 8:1 "in the third year"; Scripture gives no length.
NABONIDUS, HIS FATHER (DOUGHERTY 1929)
Nabonidus's reign: 17 years.
DRIVER (1900)
Nabonidus's reign; Driver held that Belshazzar was "the king's son", not king.
Nebuchadnezzar, as Daniel says
Daniel 5
The queen speaks of "the king Nebuchadnezzar thy father", and Daniel says "thou his son, O Belshazzar". Daniel 5:11 Daniel 5:22
"Father" means grandfather
the Geneva Bible notes (1599); Matthew Poole (1683–85); Joseph Benson (1811–18)

The Geneva note on Daniel 5:2: "Meaning his grandfather". Poole says he "might be called his son though his grandson", citing Jeremiah 27:7 ("him, and his son, and his son's son"); Benson makes him the son of Evil-merodach. Daniel 5:2 Jeremiah 27:7 [42][60][59]
Son of Nabonidus, by the inscriptions
the Babylonian inscriptions; R. W. Rogers (1912)
Nabonidus calls Belshazzar "the first-born son, the issue of my body".[91]
Nebuchadnezzar's grandson through his mother
R. P. Dougherty (1929); allowed as a possibility by S. R. Driver (1900)

Dougherty argued, from a chain of circumstantial evidence, that Nabonidus's wife Nitocris was a daughter of Nebuchadnezzar, so that Belshazzar was Nebuchadnezzar's grandson. Driver allowed the possibility, but noted that no inscription of Nabonidus implies any tie to Nebuchadnezzar, and that Daniel 5 gives the "impression that in the view of the writer Belshazzar was actually Nebuchadnezzar's son".[69][95]
A royal predecessor called "father"
R. D. Wilson (1915)
Wilson: either one was his real and the other his adoptive father, or the greatest of his predecessors is called his father, "just as Omri is called by the Assyrians the father of Jehu".[64]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Daniel does not name Nabonidus.
Scripture does not say who killed Belshazzar or how.
Scripture gives no length for his reign.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textDaniel calls Nebuchadnezzar his father (Daniel 5:2, 11, 13, 18, 22), and the site's person record lists Nebuchadnezzar as his parent on that basis. The Babylonian inscriptions name Nabonidus as his father; the views are set out below. Daniel 5:2 Daniel 5:11 Daniel 5:18
